summary: Cellular IPv6→IPv4 handover breaks SSE resume: truncated closing JSON and duplicated trailing metadata
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported that when their mobile app routes switch mid-stream from IPv6 to IPv4 (typical on some carriers and eSIM handovers) an SSE resume request returns a stream that is missing the final JSON closing object and contains a duplicated metadata chunk appended after the truncated payload. The result is a parse error on the client and a visible loss of the last 1–3 sentences of the model output.

Impact:
- Customer SkyWrite Analytics (dedicated) sees ~2% of long streaming requests drop the final sentence during cellular handover scenarios.
- Affects production traffic in us-east.
- Causes downstream parsing failures in customer parser that assume well-formed JSON at stream end.

Why this is unusual: the incident reproduces reliably only when client network stack performs an address-family switch (IPv6 -> IPv4) while the stream is active and the client attempts an SSE resume using the same session token. Other disconnect types (short TCP drops, wifi->wifi) do not reproduce the corruption.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Start a long SSE stream from the Redwood hosted API using redwood-open-13B-v1 from a mobile client on a cellular (IPv6) connection.
2) While stream is active, trigger a network handover that forces IPv4 (e.g., enable airplane mode briefly and then re-enable on a carrier that prefers IPv4, or switch to an APN that returns IPv4).
3) Client performs SSE reconnect/resume with the original X-Resume-Offset and session token.
4) Observe final stream payload from resumed connection; attempt to parse as JSON.
Expected: complete JSON document with closing brace and terminal metadata event.
Observed: truncated closing JSON, followed by a duplicate metadata block ("meta":{"session":"..."}) which appears to be a leftover from previous session mapping.
observed_behavior: Resumed stream ends with a truncated JSON body (missing closing braces and final tokens) and then one or more duplicate metadata events. Client JSON parser throws a syntax error. The model output content up to the truncation appears intact, then last sentence(s) are lost. Truncation size varies (typically 5–30 tokens).
expected_behavior: SSE resume should reconstitute stream state so that complete JSON payloads and terminal metadata are delivered exactly once and in-order, regardless of client IP/address-family changes during reconnect.
investigation_notes:
- Trace IDs collected: 7c9b8f2a-3e6d-4b2f-a1c4, f2b4a7e1-9c3d-462f-8d2a.
- Edge proxy logs show two distinct inbound connections for same session token with different client IP families within 300ms of each other.
- Resume handoff code binds an ephemeral connection mapping keyed by connection tuple; session token resume path uses both token and connection-path assertion to avoid replay.
- Hypothesis: after IPv6->IPv4 handover the edge mapping rejects the in-flight resume and creates a new stream session that merges server-side tail fragments with a stochastic ordering, leading to a partial write of the final JSON object followed by a metadata re-emit.
- No Gateway 5xx logged; backend serving runtime reports normal close-of-stream.
- KV cache priming appears unchanged; however resume offset accepted by backend differs by a single chunk boundary in multiple traces.
- Packet captures (pcap) from customer show abrupt 4-tuple change and reuse of session token on new connection without explicit connection-handshake step the server expects for atomic resume.
- Reproduced internally with a test harness that simulates AF switching; reproduced in 9/10 runs when resume performed within 1s of handover.

workaround: Advise customer to: 1) If feasible, defer automatic resume for 2s after a detected address-family change in the client network stack (this avoids the tight race window). 2) Use short keepalive heartbeats so the edge mapping ages out predictable; or 3) For critical flows set up client fallback to request a fresh, non-resume stream (new session token) when IP family changes. Support engineering provided a sample client patch that waits 2s before resume. Customer applied patch and reported no failures in a small canary (n=200 streams).
next_steps:
1) Engineering (edge team) to add detection and stricter atomicity checks when session token is reused from a different address-family within the same timeframe; investigate accepting resume only after a verified 3-way handshake equivalent.
2) Add server-side validation to avoid emitting tail fragments before confirming resume-offset atomicity; buffer terminal fragments until atomic commit.
3) Postmortem documentation and a short runbook entry for customers on mobile networks explaining recommended client behavior for resume after network handover.
4) Patch ETA: design notes by 2026-03-15, PR by 2026-03-22.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Liam Rodriguez (Support): Customer reported repeated JSON parse failures when mobile users lose the last sentence on resume. Repro steps and pcaps attached. Assigned to Priya.

2026-03-11 - Priya Kapoor (SRE): Confirmed reproduction in lab with AF switch harness. Captured resume offset mismatch and two connection events. Hypothesizing edge-proxy bind-by-connection mapping is the root cause.

2026-03-11 - Arun Patel (Edge Eng): Looking at edge mapping logic; we currently allow token-based resume but still assume consistent connection tuple for ordering guarantees. Will propose making resume acceptance stricter for address-family changes.
2026-03-12 - Customer (SkyWrite): Applied client workaround to delay resume by 2s; initial canary of 200 long streams showed 0/200 failures. Thank you, will monitor 24h and report back.
2026-03-13 - Priya Kapoor (SRE): Created internal test PR to add an AF-change guard and buffered-tail commit. Linked PR in related_github_prs. Marking as In Progress until PR review complete.
